title: State of Tamil Nadu v. Gowri Shankar @ Auto Shankar & Ors.
crime_type: Serial Kidnapping / Contract Homicide / Wall Concealment
court_or_authority: Supreme Court of India / High Court of Madras / Sessions Court Chengalpattu
source: Supreme Court of India Official Judgment & Indian Kanoon (doc/1218204)
ipc_sections: Section 201 IPC (Disappearance of evidence - concealment behind residential masonry)
evidence: Demolition and forensic recovery of human skeletal remains buried beneath concrete kitchen flooring and inside plastered wall cavities of Shankar's residence
Forensic superimposition photo identification linking excavated skulls to missing teenage girls and illicit liquor associates
Recovery of an autorickshaw (registration MSW 3786) customized with reinforced passenger locks used for abductions
Co-accused confession under Section 164 CrPC identifying burial spots and execution method
Recovery of victim gold ear studs and wristwatches from local pawn brokers
modus_operandi: Operated an autorickshaw fleet connected to illicit prostitution and moonshine networks. Picked up victims under pretext of transport, abducted young women resisting trafficking, and liquidated business rivals. Drugged victims, strangled them inside rented beach houses, cremated or buried remains under newly cast cement flooring inside his home, and whitewashed the walls.
personality_disorder: Clinical and criminological assessment documented psychopathy, extreme power and dominance fixation, predatory sexual aggression, and coercive antisocial leadership.
common_traits: Use of commercial auto-rickshaws as abduction vehicles
Auto-rickshaw fleet operation for illicit liquor transport
Covert concealment of victims' remains under concrete masonry inside home
Burying bodies under residential concrete floors and cement plaster
Targeting marginalized women and underworld rivals
Coordination with familial and local criminal gang affiliates
Intimidation of local neighborhood through claimed political and police patronage
summary: Historic Chennai serial murder investigation involving six victims between 1987 and 1988. The Supreme Court confirmed capital punishment for Auto Shankar and two accomplices, making it a foundational Indian legal precedent on corpus delicti and recovery under Section 27 Evidence Act.
